ledger.title: Evidence Acquisition: survey spacing 5 mm -> 2 mm
ledger.why: 133 missed at every budget (recall is flat 0.664 at 0.25/0.5/1/2 FP). - not seen: 0.3% (1 lesion) - seen, not recognized: 28.8% - inconsistently recognized (found by a sibling seed only): 4.5% - recognized, then rejected: 0.0% The reader produces only 0.18 FP/scan in total (24 FP clusters across 130 scans), so the FP budget up to 2/scan is unused; every candidate it reports is kept. Misses concentrate in small lesions: 0.1–0.3 mL detected 44% (n=185), shown on 1.6 survey slices on average; 0.3–1 mL 79% (2.4 slices); >1 mL >= 92%.
ledger.hypothesis: small lesions are missed mainly because they get only ~1–2 looks at 5 mm spacing and per-slice recognition is unreliable. Reading at 2 mm spacing (step 2 slices at 1 mm, every slice at 1.5 mm) gives each small lesion ~2.5x more views, so P(found on >= 1 slice) rises; extra FPs are affordable because the budget is barely used and support (#slices) ranking should keep isolated FPs below multi-slice true lesions.
ledger.predicted: recall_any +5 to +10 pts, mostly 0.1–1 mL; FP/scan rises to ~0.5–1; J +0.03 to +0.07.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 1: ACCEPT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = +0.0284 > 0; every seed dJ > 0: yes).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: T1c peak-intensity tie-break within support
ledger.why: - b=0.25: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 23.7%, inconsistent 4.0%, rejected 9.6% (recall 0.626) - b=0.5/1/2: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 23.7%, inconsistent 4.0%, rejected 0.0% (recall 0.722) The 9.6% rejected at b=0.25 are support-1 hits tied with support-1 FPs (s20: 40 hits vs 34 FPs at support 1); the whole tie group exceeds 0.25 FP/scan, so none can be admitted. Diagnostic (scripts/diag_support1.py): peak normalised T1c intensity in a 5x5 patch at the candidate is higher for support-1 hits than FPs on all seeds (medians hit/FP: s20 0.82/0.66, s21 0.82/0.75, s22 0.85/0.72) — enhancing metastases are bright on T1c.
ledger.hypothesis: ranking ties within support by T1c peak intensity (score = support + 0.01 freq + 0.5 * peak; support stays primary) lets the brighter half of support-1 candidates in under 0.25 FP/scan, recovering part of the rejected 9.6% at b=0.25. (The dominant cause, not recognized 23.7%, is targeted next round by retraining; this cheap round goes first so the next round is matched to it.)
ledger.predicted: recall@0.25 +2 to +5 pts on s20, other budgets unchanged; dJ +0.005 to +0.012.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 2: ACCEPT** (trial.py seed 0 s20: J 0.6982 -> 0.7216, dJ = +0.0234 > 0; bootstrap P(dJ>0) 0.848, CI [0.000, +0.032]).

ledger.title: Visual Representation: render at 768 px long side (was 384), retrain SFT + read
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 23.7%, inconsistent 4.0%, rejected 0.0% (0.3% at b=0.25). Recall 0.720–0.722. FP use is only 0.23–0.30/scan of the 2 allowed. Misses are small lesions: 0.1–0.3 mL detected 52% (n=185) although each is shown on 4.3 slices; >1 mL >= 92%. The reader looks at small lesions but does not recognise them. Evidence on representation: at 384 px a 0.1–0.3 mL lesion spans ~13 px (10th–90th pct 11–16 px), while Qwen3-VL's merged visual token covers 32x32 px (patch 16, merge 2), i.e. the lesion is < 1/4 of one token (120 tokens per slice image).
ledger.hypothesis: small metastases are not recognised because they are sub-token at 384 px. Rendering at 768 px (504 tokens per image, lesion ~26 px) gives the vision encoder features for them. The reader must be retrained at the new resolution (same SFT recipe, data data/sft/train_t1c_L768 = same views/targets as train_t1c re-rendered at 768).
ledger.predicted: 0.1–0.3 mL detection 52% -> 60–70%; recall_any +4 to +8 pts; FP/scan may rise but stays << 2; J +0.03 to +0.07.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 3: ACCEPT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = +0.0495 > 0; every seed dJ > 0: yes).

ledger.title: Evidence Acquisition: 4 extra sampled reads per view (T=1.0) merged with the greedy read, ranked by #(slice,sample) reports
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 17.9%, inconsistent 4.5%, rejected 0.0% (0.3% at b=0.25). Recall 0.775. FP/scan used: 0.30 of 2 allowed (0.18–0.30 across seeds), so recall is limited by what the greedy reader will report, not by ranking. Small lesions dominate: 0.1–0.3 mL detected 60% (68% by some seed), shown on 4.3 slices each. The 4.5% "inconsistent" lesions (found by another seed's reader) show the report/no-report decision is near threshold for some lesions; greedy decoding hides this probability mass.
ledger.hypothesis: sampling the reader at T=1.0 exposes low-confidence reports that greedy decoding suppresses. Union of greedy + 4 sampled reads (5 samples) adds true small lesions; ranking by the number of (slice, sample) reports (cfg rank "pairs") keeps the greedy-consistent findings on top, and the new low-evidence candidates fill the unused FP budget.
ledger.predicted: recall_any +3 to +6 pts; FP/scan up to ~1–2; recall at 1–2 FP gains most, at 0.25 roughly unchanged; J +0.01 to +0.03.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 4: REJECT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = -0.0023 <= 0; every seed dJ > 0: no).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: greedy-first ranking, sampled-only clusters appended below
ledger.why: r3 as in round 4 (s20: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 17.9%, inconsistent 4.5%, rejected 0.0–0.3%; FP use 0.18–0.30/scan of 2). New evidence from round 4's saved sampled reads (s20): 44 lesions are reported only by sampled reads at locations > 12 mm from every greedy candidate, i.e. part of the "not recognized"/"inconsistent" loss is recognised at T=1 but suppressed by greedy decoding. Round 4 lost because its pairs ranking demoted greedy single-slice hits below multi-sample FP clusters (recall@0.25 0.773 -> 0.742), not because the extra candidates were useless (recall@2 +2 pts).
ledger.hypothesis: keep the r3 report exactly (greedy-read candidates, same clustering, same order; verified identical: 406/406) as a top tier, and append sampled-only clusters (no greedy candidate within merge_mm=12 mm), ranked by #(slice,sample) reports + T1c peak tie-break. The curve then equals r3's up to r3's FP total and extends it into the unused budget.
ledger.predicted: recall@0.25 unchanged; recall@0.5/1/2 +1 to +3 pts; J +0.005 to +0.02.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 5: ACCEPT** (3-seed rule: mean dJ = +0.0438 > 0; every seed dJ > 0: yes; seed-0 trial.py dJ = +0.0436 > 0 also).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: sampled confirmation as tie-break within greedy support
ledger.why: | budget | recall | not seen | not recognized | inconsistent | rejected | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0.25 | 0.773 | 0.0% | 8.1% | 4.3% | 10.4% | | 0.5 | 0.818 | 0.0% | 8.1% | 4.3% | 5.8% | | 1 | 0.836 | 0.0% | 8.1% | 4.3% | 4.0% | | 2 | 0.846 | 0.0% | 8.1% | 4.3% | 3.0% | Rejected is now the largest single cause averaged over budgets (5.8%), concentrated at 0.25–0.5 FP. Diagnostics (diag_tiers.py, diag_confirm.py, all seeds): greedy support >= 2 candidates are ~93–100% precise; greedy support-1 candidates are 45–68% precise and form the tie group straddling the 0.25 budget. Among them, those confirmed by >= 4 sampled (slice,sample) reports within 6 mm are 61–81% precise vs ~27–64% for less-confirmed ones, on all three seeds.
ledger.hypothesis: ordering greedy candidates within a support level by sampled confirmation (score += 0.04*min(confirm,10); with peak 0.5 the tie-break stays < 1 so support remains primary and tiers unchanged) admits the more reliable support-1 hits first under the 0.25/0.5 budgets.
ledger.predicted: recall@0.25 +1 to +3 pts, other budgets ~unchanged; dJ +0.003 to +0.01.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 6: REJECT** (trial.py seed 0 s20: J 0.8182 -> 0.8176, dJ = -0.0006 <= 0; bootstrap P(dJ>0) 0.13).

ledger.title: Visual Representation: render at 1152 px long side (was 768), retrain SFT + re-read
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 8.1%, inconsistent 4.3% at all budgets; rejected 10.4/5.8/4.0/3.0% at 0.25/0.5/1/2. Round 6 showed the greedy tier's ranking is close to exhausted: the rejected loss is a precision limit of weak (support-1) greedy reports. Of the lesions missed at 2 FP, 85% are < 0.3 mL (median 0.16 mL, ~6.8 mm diameter); at 768 px that is ~26–30 px, about one 32x32 px merged visual token. The 384 -> 768 step (round 3) raised 0.1–0.3 mL detection from 52% to 60% (greedy) and gave dJ +0.05.
ledger.hypothesis: small lesions are still at the resolution limit of the vision encoder. Rendering at 1152 px (~1130 tokens per image, small lesion ~40–45 px) makes them more recognisable (fewer not recognized / inconsistent). It also makes weak reports more reliable, so more true small lesions reach support >= 2 and the 0.25 budget is less limited (less rejected).
ledger.predicted: recall_any +2 to +4 pts; recall@0.25 +2 to +5 pts; J +0.01 to +0.03.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 7: REJECT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = -0.0118 <= 0; every seed dJ > 0: no).

ledger.title: Learning Policy: group-relative policy-gradient RL on top of the 768 px SFT reader
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%; not recognized 8.1%; inconsistent 4.3%; rejected 10.4/5.8/4.0/3.0% at 0.25/0.5/1/2 FP. Learnability census on r5's sampled reads (G=4, T=1, per seed s20/s21/s22): never detected 10.4/10.6/13.1%, frontier (1–3 of 4 samples) 22.5/22.0/20.2%, always 67%; r_t = 0.69/0.67/0.61. The frontier is almost all 0.1–1 mL lesions (26–30% of them). So most of the remaining loss is inconsistent recognition: the reader assigns the lesion some probability but greedy decoding drops it (inconsistent / rejected as weak sampled-only evidence). Round 7 showed that more pixels do not help; rounds 6 showed re-ranking is exhausted.
ledger.hypothesis: RL with the evaluation's own hit geometry (point within 5 mm of a lesion mask) sharpens frontier lesions into consistent reports. Reward per sampled report = #distinct >= 0.1 mL lesions hit - 1.0 * #points not within 5 mm of any lesion (-1 if unparsable); group-mean baseline over G=4 samples; 600 steps x 16 train views (50% with a >= 0.1 mL lesion within 5 mm, 50% lesion-free); T=1.0; lr 1e-5; LoRA initialised from the r5 SFT adapter (scripts/rl.py, geometry from make_rl.py).
ledger.predicted: greedy recall_any +2 to +5 pts (frontier -> always); recall@0.25 +2 to +4 pts; J +0.01 to +0.03. Risk: FP penalty could make the reader more conservative on uncertain views.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 8: ACCEPT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = +0.0179 > 0; every seed dJ > 0: yes).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: two-reader report (RL reader + its SFT parent, same seed) on saved reads
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 8.1%, inconsistent 4.3% at every budget, rejected 7.3/4.0/2.3/0.3% at 0.25/0.5/1/2. Two rounds of evidence show the RL reader is sensitive but imprecise at low support (greedy support-1 precision 9–25%), while its SFT parent (r5 reads, same seed) was conservative and precise (support-1 precision 45–68%). New evidence (s20): of the 78 lesions r8 misses at 0.25 FP/scan, 35 are found by the SFT reads (13 by the SFT greedy read); at 2 FP, 11 of 50. Union recall_any RL+SFT = 0.904 vs RL alone 0.876. So part of the not-recognized/inconsistent/rejected loss is reader-specific, and the two readers' agreement is evidence the single-reader ranking does not use.
ledger.hypothesis: a report built from both readers of the same seed is better. Top tier = candidates clustered jointly from the RL greedy read and the SFT greedy read, ranked by #(slice, read) reports, so agreement of the two readers counts double and SFT-only greedy findings enter the top tier; lower tier = clusters from the 8 sampled reads (4 RL + 4 SFT) more than 12 mm from any top-tier candidate, ranked by #(slice, sample) reports; T1c peak tie-break as before.

ledger.title: Visual Representation: 2.5D colour encoding of through-plane context (R/G/B = slice -3 mm / 0 / +3 mm)
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 8.1%, inconsistent 4.3% at every budget; rejected 7.3/4.0/2.3/0.3% at 0.25/0.5/1/2. The rejected loss comes from low-precision weak greedy reports (support-1 precision 9–25%), i.e. the reader cannot tell many small bright in-plane spots apart from metastases. The not-recognized loss is small lesions (85% < 0.3 mL). Three different routes have now failed to move this: more pixels (r7: no gain beyond 768 px), more RL (r9: reward plateau), and re-ranking or combining readers (r6, r10: FPs and hits not separable from the reports). A single axial slice lacks the cue radiologists use for small enhancing foci: through-plane shape. A metastasis is a compact sphere, while a vessel or sulcal/dural enhancement continues across slices.
ledger.hypothesis: giving the reader through-plane context at no token cost improves both recognition of small metastases and precision of weak reports. Each view is one RGB image: G = the slice itself (identical to the current grey image), R = slice 3 mm below, B = slice 3 mm above (render protocol 't1crgb', prompt names the colour code). Uniform tissue stays grey (close to the pretrained distribution); a small sphere centred on the slice appears as a green-dominant dot; through-plane structures appear white/grey.
ledger.predicted: greedy support-1 precision up and fewer FPs at low budgets; recall@0.25/0.5 +1 to +3 pts; not recognized -1 to -2 pts; J +0.01 to +0.02.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 11: REJECT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = -0.0164 <= 0; every seed dJ > 0: no).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: merge radius 12 mm -> 6 mm on the accepted reads
ledger.why: failures.py gives not seen 0.0%, not recognized 8.1%, inconsistent 4.3%, rejected 7.3/4.0/2.3/0.3% at 0.25/0.5/1/2. New evidence: failures.py classifies after clustering, so "not recognized" includes lesions that were reported but lost when their points were clustered. scripts/diag_pointloss.py checks the raw reported points: of the 50 lesions missed at 2 FP/scan, 19 have a greedy-read point within 5 mm of the mask (23 a point from some read); at 0.25 FP/scan, 39 of 78. With single-linkage clustering at merge_mm = 12 mm, reports of a small lesion chain into a neighbouring cluster (another lesion or nearby FP reports). The cluster's medoid then lies > 5 mm from the lesion, so the lesion is never a hit. About 5% of recall is lost by aggregation, not by the reader.
ledger.hypothesis: a merge radius of 6 mm (chosen a priori, no sweep) keeps clusters compact relative to the 5 mm hit tolerance. It still links one lesion's reports on adjacent 2 mm survey slices (typically 2–4 mm apart in 3D). Extra candidates on the same true lesion are harmless (not FPs); the cost is that some FP clusters split and per-candidate support shrinks.
ledger.predicted: recall at 1–2 FP +2 to +4 pts; at 0.25 roughly unchanged (more, smaller FP candidates compete); J +0.005 to +0.02.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 12: ACCEPT** (trial.py seed 0 s20: J 0.8415 -> 0.8725, dJ = +0.0309 > 0; bootstrap P(dJ>0) 0.9995, CI [+0.011, +0.056]).

ledger.title: Evidence Acquisition: greedy read on every slice (spacing 1 mm) instead of 2 mm
ledger.why: | budget | recall | not seen | not recognized | inconsistent | rejected | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0.25 | 0.826 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 9.1% | | 0.5 | 0.864 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 5.3% | | 1 | 0.889 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 2.8% | | 2 | 0.912 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 0.5% | Clustering loss is now small (diag_pointloss: 5 of 35 lesions missed at 2 FP have a greedy point within 5 mm, was 19 of 50). Rejected (averaged over budgets 4.4%) is the largest term. Its cause (diag_tiers, diag_frag): greedy support-1 candidates are 21–39% precise and are almost all isolated (s20: 122 of 127 support-1 FPs and 24 of 27 support-1 new-lesion hits lie > 12 mm from any stronger candidate; s21 similar). So weak true reports and single-slice FP reports are indistinguishable by position or support at 2 mm sampling.
ledger.hypothesis: reading every slice gives each small lesion about twice as many greedy looks in the 1 mm studies (1.5 mm studies are already read on every slice). A lesion >= 0.1 mL (>= ~6 mm) is reported on consecutive slices and climbs to support >= 2, and inconsistently recognised lesions get more chances. Single-slice FP reports, which do not repeat on the neighbouring slice, stay at support 1. This separates the support-1 tie group, as 5 -> 2 mm did in round 1.
ledger.predicted: recall@0.25/0.5 +1 to +3 pts, recall@2 ~+1 pt; J +0.005 to +0.015. Risk: more FP views in 1 mm studies.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 13: REJECT** (seed_rule: mean dJ = -0.0015 <= 0; every seed dJ > 0: no).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: 3D Hessian blobness replaces T1c peak intensity as the within-support tie-break
ledger.why: not seen 0.0%, not recognized 5.3%, inconsistent 3.0%; rejected 9.1/5.3/2.8/0.5% at 0.25/0.5/1/2 FP/scan. Rejected is the largest term at low budgets: true weak reports (greedy support 1–2) are tied with FP reports and ordered only by peak T1c intensity. Rounds 6, 10 and 13 showed that the reports themselves (sampled confirmation, a second reader, denser slices) do not separate them, and diag_frag showed that position does not either (FPs are isolated). Image evidence does (scripts/diag_blob.py): 3D Hessian blobness at the candidate (sigma 2 mm; sigma^2 * -(sum of eigenvalues) when all eigenvalues are negative, i.e. a bright compact structure, times isotropy |l_min|/|l_max|, which is ~1 for a sphere and ~0 for a vessel or plane; max within 3 mm) separates hits from FPs with AUC 0.79/0.65/0.73 at support 1 and 0.74/0.77/0.77 at support 2 (s20/s21/s22). Peak intensity reaches only 0.62/0.5
ledger.hypothesis: ordering candidates within each support level (and within tier 0's report counts) by blobness instead of peak intensity puts weak true metastasis reports ahead of tubular or planar FP reports, so more true lesions fit under the 0.25–1 FP budgets.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 14: ACCEPT** (trial.py seed 0 s20: J 0.8725 -> 0.8870, dJ = +0.0145 > 0; bootstrap P(dJ>0) 0.992, CI [+0.002, +0.022]).

ledger.title: Decision Aggregation: one evidence scale for greedy and sampled-only candidates (sampled report = 1/G greedy report)
ledger.why: | budget | recall | FP/scan used | not seen | not recognized | inconsistent | rejected | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0.25 | 0.864 | 0.24 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 5.3% | | 0.5 | 0.881 | 0.48 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 3.5% | | 1 | 0.889 | 0.64 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 2.8% | | 2 | 0.914 | 1.96 | 0.0% | 5.3% | 3.0% | 0.3% | At 1 FP/scan only 0.64 FP/scan is used: after that point the ranking runs through greedy support-1 low-blobness reports (diag_blobtiers: precision 0.08/0.14/0.16 on s20/s21/s22). The strict tier wall puts these above every sampled-only cluster, including those with >= 2 sampled reports and high blobness (precision 0.20–0.75), so the 2.8% rejected at 1 FP are mostly sampled-only true lesions stuck behind greedy junk. (Clustering loss stays small: 5 of 34 missed at 2 FP have a greedy point within 5 mm.)
ledger.hypothesis: ranking both tiers on one scale, with each sampled-only report counting 1/G = 1/4 of a greedy slice report (a sampled read is one of G draws, so pairs/G is its expected support per read) plus the same blobness tie-break, lets strong sampled-only findings pass weak, non-blob greedy reports. Greedy candidates keep their clusters and their order relative to each other.
ledger.predicted: recall@1 +1 to +2 pts, @0.5 +0 to +1, @0.25 and @2 ~unchanged; dJ +0.002 to +0.008.
ledger.outcome: Outcome round 15: ACCEPT** (trial.py seed 0 s20: J 0.8870 -> 0.8889, dJ = +0.0019 > 0; bootstrap P(dJ>0) 0.825, CI [0.000, +0.004]).
